claims.text: Applying surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) to a coarse-grained alloy creates a gradient nanostructured surface layer.
SMAT treatment produces a concurrent improvement in strength and ductility.
The proposed initial material is a coarse-grained high-strength steel or aluminum alloy with a conventional strength-ductility balance.
Controlled SMAT induces a grain-size gradient from a nanostructured treated surface to an untouched coarse-grained core.
Room-temperature SMAT in ambient atmosphere can produce a continuous microstructural gradient across the sample thickness when duration and impact energy are optimized.
The resulting microstructure has a hard nanograined surface that gradually transitions to a more ductile coarse-grained core.
The nanostructured surface layer contains a high density of grain boundaries.
The high density of grain boundaries hinders dislocation motion.
Dislocation hindrance in the nanostructured surface layer increases yield strength.
Dislocation hindrance in the nanostructured surface layer increases ultimate tensile strength.
The coarse-grained core retains plastic-deformation capacity.
Plastic deformation in the coarse-grained core preserves or enhances the overall ductility of the treated sample.
SMAT-treated samples will have higher yield strength than untreated coarse-grained controls.
SMAT-treated samples will have higher ultimate tensile strength than untreated coarse-grained controls.
SMAT-treated samples will maintain or improve total elongation relative to untreated controls.
The strength-ductility benefit is sensitive to SMAT duration and impact energy.
Excessive or insufficient SMAT may fail to produce an optimal microstructural gradient.
The beneficial effect may diminish under cyclic loading.
The beneficial effect may diminish in alloys with very low workability.

contradictions.description: The untreated starting alloy is characterized as a 'high-strength alloy' in the initial-state field but as having only 'moderate strength levels' in the baseline field. The relative reference for these terms is not specified.
